title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM: Preventing Sensitive Data Exposure
practice: Take a sample incoming customer email or ticket and manually redact all direct identifiers (names, emails, phone numbers, and account IDs) into tokens like [CUSTOMER_NAME] before drafting an AI prompt.
success_measure: Verify that zero customer PII or raw internal identifiers appear in your prompt history.

title: De-identification & Masking Best Practices for Sensitive Data
practice: List the top 3 types of data you handle daily. Create a personal 1-page reference cheat-sheet categorizing each into 'Safe for AI', 'Mask Before Prompting', and 'Strictly Prohibited'.
success_measure: Have a clear, team-aligned list of prohibited data attributes posted near your workstation.

title: Best Practices for Reviewing and Verifying AI-Generated Code
practice: Ask an AI assistant to generate a utility function with data parsing. Write at least two automated edge-case unit tests (e.g., null input, empty array, unicode characters) without asking the AI.
success_measure: Identify and document at least one unhandled edge case or assumption made by the AI before merging.

title: Effective Use and Rigorous Testing of AI Coding Tools
practice: Pick a legacy function and prompt an AI to refactor it. Review the diff line-by-line for subtle semantic drifts, unexpected performance bottlenecks, or altered variable scopes.
success_measure: Confirm that all existing regression tests pass and that the refactored code introduces no new dependencies.

title: Structured Prompt Engineering & Output Verification Guide
practice: Rewrite a vague one-sentence task prompt into a structured prompt using 4 sections: <Context>, <Task>, <Constraints>, and <Expected Output Format>.
success_measure: The structured prompt generates a consistent, factual output matching your schema across 3 separate test runs.

title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)
provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
practice: Review your department's most common AI use cases against the NIST 'Govern' and 'Map' pillars. Draft three clear team rules regarding acceptable tools, output verification, and client transparency.
success_measure: Produce a 3-bullet AI governance agreement approved by your team or leadership.

title: Principles for the Security and Verification of AI Systems
practice: Check your local development environment to ensure that API keys, session tokens, and proprietary credentials are never stored in plain text or passed as prompt context.
success_measure: Verify that your repository's .gitignore properly excludes all local secrets and environment configuration.

title: Trusted AI for Customer Outreach and Sales Intelligence
practice: Take an AI-generated outbound sales message and fact-check all product capability statements against your actual product documentation.
success_measure: Remove or correct any unverified claims or exaggerated performance metrics before sending.
